learning_outcomes.text: Students will possess broad and integrated knowledge and understanding of techniques in heating and air conditioning technology and for refrigeration machines and heat pumps.

Students will have a critical understanding of the scientific and technical methods needed for the development of systems and components and can evaluate the results regarding the underlying requirements.
Students will have extensive scientific-technical knowledge, which they apply to special applications in the field of heating, refrigeration, and air conditioning technology.
Students will know the components of these systems, be able to combine them for different requirements, calculate the overall processes, and evaluate optimization possibilities.
Students will be able to assess the conception of a heating, refrigeration, or air conditioning system and make evidence-based, qualitative, and quantitative judgments on its use.
Students will use various standard and advanced procedures, methods, and engineering guidelines to obtain and process system-relevant data.
Students will prepare data, generate results with suitable calculation methods, and present them in a structured way.
The information and results obtained will be applied to systems to be designed in heating, refrigeration, and air conditioning technology.

Students will conduct application-oriented practicals in small groups, where they examine the structure and function of relevant components and systems in detail and jointly develop and implement solutions for specific use cases.
Students will be able to balance and evaluate components and systems based on measurement data.

assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 3 experiments. The duration and scope of the graded assessment are subject to the current study regulations.
